question: How much rock core was drilled to map the Turin–Lyon tunnel's geology?
answer: Along the Turin–Lyon route, every cylinder of rock core pulled up was examined. Together they identified the rock formations, the faults and the water before digging. Laid end to end, all the core comes to about 65 km.
move: A big tunnel is first read in rock: here, about 65 km of it.

web.label: The Alps cut open between France and Italy, with the 57.5 km base tunnel through them and drill rigs on the peaks. Under them, the reader drags out a rock core to guess how long all the core drilled along the route is, laid end to end, then says how sure. The real core then runs out past the tunnel's far end: about 65 km.

source: Geopop, “TAV Torino-Lione: a che punto è? Gli aspetti tecnici di cui non si parla (quasi) mai” (YouTube, 2022)
